name: Bob Niemeyer

bio.statement: Ballotpedia says Niemeyer grew up in Silverton, Oregon, and is the son of a dentist.
bio.excerpt: Niemeyer is the son of a dentist and grew up in Silverton, Oregon.

bio.statement: Ballotpedia says he is a licensed professional mechanical engineer who founded his own engineering company in 1988.
bio.excerpt: He is a licensed professional mechanical engineer and, in 1988, founded his own engineering company.

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Niemeyer lists his occupation as engineer and president of New Ventures Engineering.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Engineer Occupational Background: President New Ventures Engineering

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

bio.statement: Niemeyer lists a BS in mechanical engineering from Oregon State University and registered professional engineer status.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: BS Mecahnical Engineering Oregon State University, Registered Professional Engineer

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

bio.statement: Niemeyer lists mentoring the Tigard High School First Robotics program as his prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Mentor Tigard HS First Robotics Program

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Niemeyer says in-person voting with photo ID is the only way to get government to listen to citizens again.
positions.excerpt: The only way to get our government to listen to American Citizens again is in-person voting with photo ID.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Niemeyer says toll roads are an example of government not listening to people, and that tolls are only necessary to fund government.
positions.excerpt: Toll roads are the next example of NOT listening to the People because tolls are only necessary to fund government, not our roads.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Niemeyer says state fees, taxes and regulations on new housing construction amount to deficit spending.
positions.excerpt: Our government has also found ways to “deficit-spend” with fees, taxes, and regulations on all new construction of housing.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Niemeyer cites the successful effort to stop the gas tax as evidence that government is not listening to people.
positions.excerpt: We ALL know how we successfully stopped the Gas Tax.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

gaps: No 2026 policy positions found; Ballotpedia lists none for 2026 and he did not complete its 2026 survey
